headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/capability conflict: Haystack can use MCP and broad egress while Notion AI accesses shared workspace content and vendor backends.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, and Notion AI reads workspace pages/databases in a shared workspace. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Notion content is fed into Haystack or vice versa. The profiles do not prove direct default ingestion, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Notion page content is passed into Haystack prompts or MCP tools without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF Haystack outputs are copied into Notion pages and later treated as instructions, the bridge exists.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from Notion pages into Haystack.
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent content.
Require human review before executing any MCP-derived instruction.
Restrict Haystack to read-only retrieval for Notion-sourced text.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction/ მონაცემ separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call external APIs; Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion backends/downstream model providers. If the pair shares workspace data, sensitive page content can flow through both systems and leave the workspace. The profiles do not show PHI or secrets, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF the same workspace pages are routed into Haystack and Notion AI, both systems can process the same content.
IF those pages contain sensitive business data, the data leaves the local workspace boundary.
mitigations: Limit both agents to non-sensitive pages.
Turn off Haystack connectors that forward full documents externally.
Use a separate workspace for sensitive material.
Review Notion AI usage on restricted pages before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any external API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can use MCP and external APIs, while Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances and limited Notion-controlled actions. Their mutable surfaces overlap on workspace content, so concurrent edits or conflicting writes are plausible even though Notion AI cannot write the host filesystem. The shared workspace model makes this a default coordination risk.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same Notion page or database in one session window, last-write conflicts can occur.
IF Haystack writes back through an MCP-connected workflow into the same workspace, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only on shared pages.
Use page-level ownership conventions.
Pause concurrent edits during agent runs.
Add optimistic-lock checks before writes.
requires-engineering: implement workspace transaction/locking support.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it can present Haystack-produced text as authoritative if that text is inserted into the workspace. Haystack can also retrieve and re-use Notion content through MCP or APIs. The profiles do not show downstream action-taking, so the main risk is unverified propagation, not irreversible action.
conditions: IF Haystack-generated summaries are pasted into Notion and later queried, Notion may treat them as grounded facts.
IF Notion answers are fed back into Haystack without verification, errors can compound across turns.
mitigations: Mark agent-generated content as unverified.
Require source links for any factual claim.
Insert a human verification step before reuse.
Separate draft and authoritative pages.
requires-engineering: add citation validation and confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are docs-only and appear to operate on workspace content, but the profiles do not show a residency mismatch, regulated data class, or certification gap. Notion AI has vendor-hosted processing and Haystack has broad egress, yet no specific compliance breach is evidenced. The other agent is cited because the risk concerns their combined handling of workspace data.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into Notion AI or Haystack without a DPA/residency review, compliance risk increases.
IF retention settings differ between the workspace and Haystack-connected storage, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review retention settings for the workspace.
Confirm vendor DPAs before enabling sensitive content.
Restrict access to approved regions only.
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls centrally.
